ai.description: The Aloysii Pond Frog (Dicroglossidae) measures 30–45 mm. It is olive-brown with dark spots and a white belly. It features a pointed snout, distinct webbing on the toes, and a prominent vocal sac.
ai.identificationRemarks: The *Euphlyctis aloysii* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, bright yellow or orange patch on its groin and the hidden surfaces of its thighs.
ai.habitat: *Euphlyctis aloysii* inhabits freshwater bodies like ponds and paddy fields in the humid tropical lowlands of the Western Ghats, typically below 500 meters in elevation.
ai.behavior: The Aloysii pond frog is primarily nocturnal, actively hunting for small insects and invertebrates near water bodies under the cover of darkness.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Euphlyctis aloysii* breeds during the monsoon, laying eggs in small, temporary water bodies. Females produce clutches of several hundred small, pigmented eggs.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Aloysii Pond Frog is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, primarily found in the states of Kerala and Karnataka at low to moderate elevations.
ai.callDescription: The Aloysii Pond Frog produces a series of rapid, high-pitched "tink-tink" notes, typically heard emanating from shallow, vegetated freshwater ponds and marshes.
